To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nuclear star formation is present in 45% of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 galaxies at a median projected scale of 65 pc and that the SFR per unit area in these nuclear regions is much higher than in circumnuclear (0.6 kpc) regions.

(1) the nuclear SFRs in the central 60-80 pc of nearby Seyfert galaxies are on average five times lower than the circumnuclear SFRs on scales of ~600 pc, (2) the nuclear SFr densities in these galaxies are on average 20 times higher than their circumnuclear SFr densities, and (3) the nuclear SFe are correlated with the black hole accreting rates.

the nuclear SFRs and Ṁ_ BH of Seyfert nuclei are tightly correlated, and this relation is consistent with the predictions of numerical simulations of the coevolution of the black hole and the host galaxy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the nuclear star-forming activity and the connection of nuclear star formation with black hole accretions in Seyfert galaxies.
understanding how star formation in the nuclear region of Seyferts is affected by AGN activity.
the physical connection between nuclear star formation and black hole accretions in Seyfert galaxies and the possible role of star formation in the feeding of the black hole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear SFR is a function of Ṁ_( BH).
the nuclear SFR in Seyfert galaxies appears to be regulated by the AGN activity.
the SFR in the central ~60 pc of Seyfert 2 galaxies is suppressed by a factor of ~5 compared with the circumnuclear regions, and this suppression is correlated with the black hole growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear SFR in Seyfert galaxies appears to be regulated by the AGN activity.
the star formation and black hole accretions are closely linked in Seyfert galaxies, but the star formation activity is suppressed on scales larger than ~65 pc.
the nuclear SFRs and the Ṁ_(B H) are connected, but this connection does not imply a physical connection between nuclear star formation and the accretion disk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear SFRs and Ṁ_ BHs are not independent, and that nuclear SF is not suppressed in Seyfert galaxies on scales of 65 pc.
the star formation and accretion activity are connected in Seyfert galaxies, which is consistent with the idea that the gas reservoir that feeds both processes is a common entity.
the SFR in the central ~60-70 pc region of Seyfers galaxies is higher than the average SFR of the galaxy as a whole.
